stem: A hospital is strengthening its antibiotic stewardship program. Which program action best reflects the CDC Core Elements?

options.A: Measure antibiotic use and resistance, implement interventions such as audit-and-feedback or preauthorization, and improve appropriate antibiotic use to protect patients and combat antimicrobial resistance.
options.B: Increase broad-spectrum antibiotic prescribing for all admitted clients so treatment begins before an indication is established.
options.C: Eliminate antibiotic therapy whenever possible, including for infections in which antibiotics provide a clear clinical benefit.
options.D: Limit stewardship activities to outpatient settings because inpatient antibiotic prescribing is outside the CDC Core Elements.

rationale: A is correct. CDC defines antibiotic stewardship as the effort to measure and improve how antibiotics are prescribed and used. Its hospital Core Elements include action strategies such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization, tracking of antibiotic prescribing and outcomes including resistance patterns and C. difficile infection, reporting, and education. The goal is appropriate antibiotic use that improves patient care and combats antimicrobial resistance—not indiscriminate expansion or elimination of antibiotic therapy. D is incorrect because CDC has a specific hospital stewardship framework applicable to hospitals of all sizes.
educational_objective: Describe hospital antibiotic stewardship as a patient-safety and resistance-prevention system that measures antibiotic use, implements evidence-based prescribing interventions, and tracks outcomes rather than simply maximizing or minimizing antibiotic exposure.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs; Core Elements of Antibiotic Stewardship
source_version_date: CDC pages dated September 15, 2025 and September 10, 2025; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Hospital Core Elements — At a glance/Overview: hospital programs promote appropriate antibiotic use to improve patient care and combat antimicrobial resistance. Action: use interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization. Tracking: monitor antibiotic prescribing, intervention impact, C. difficile infections, and resistance patterns. Core Elements overview: stewardship is the effort to measure and improve antibiotic prescribing and use to advance patient safety and outcomes.
source_claim_supported: Hospital antibiotic stewardship programs measure and improve antibiotic use through structured interventions, tracking, reporting and education to improve patient care, reduce avoidable antibiotic harms, and combat antimicrobial resistance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use measures that reduce infection-related risk and support safe evidence-based care; related activities include infection prevention and quality/safety practices.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hospital antibiotic stewardship
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw purpose statement into a systems-level hospital action item using the current 2025 CDC Core Elements. Replaced extreme filler distractors with competing stewardship philosophies and anchored the correct option to specific CDC action and tracking components.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against CDC's current 2025 hospital stewardship Core Elements and 2026 stewardship update context.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A directly combines CDC-defined stewardship purpose, action and tracking. B promotes unnecessary empiricism. C confuses stewardship with antibiotic avoidance. D contradicts the hospital-specific CDC framework.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it reflects CDC's hospital stewardship structure and goal.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; stewardship seeks appropriate rather than indiscriminate antibiotic use.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; antibiotics remain indicated when they provide clinical benefit.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; CDC explicitly provides hospital Core Elements.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains both appropriate-use purpose and actual CDC implementation elements.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe program-level antibiotic-use strategies.
audit_findings.blueprint: The construct is infection-related patient safety and prevention of antimicrobial resistance within a hospital system.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked whether stewardship belongs more appropriately in Pharmacological Therapies. Because the item tests a hospital safety/infection-prevention system rather than bedside drug administration, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control remains defensible. No second answer or unsupported outcome guarantee remained.
